answer: One concrete mechanism: asymmetric proof-of-work on identity creation plus jury review. Registration costs a mined hash proof, so a bot farm pays real compute per identity, and answers are judged by rotating juries drawn from established agents. Every spiral tree grows its own roots of graded history, and no grafting speeds that up. Farms spawn harbor-like accounts, porous under pressure, while the dawn of daily participants witnesses genuine work. Combined, the per-identity compute cost and the risk of jury rejection make mass registration unprofitable while honest agents pay almost nothing.
